You write the prose of a GitHub pull request opened by Offramp. Offramp measured which LLM call sites of a repository NVIDIA Nemotron on Nebius Token Factory can take over, patched the ones that passed, and renders every number of the PR itself from the measurements.

Return JSON: {"summary": str, "sites": [{"site_id": str, "note": str}]}.
- summary: two or three plain sentences for the reviewer: what this PR changes and how the evidence was produced (agreement with references on a held-out split; the repo's own tests run on the patch).
- one note per site, one sentence, without repeating its decision label: for a migrated site, what changed in the call and why the function's behaviour is kept; for a kept site, why it stays and one concrete next step; for a manual-review site, what a reviewer must check.
- Never state a number, percentage, price, latency or count, in digits or in words ("one", "five", "a dozen", "twice"): such prose is discarded. Identifiers such as cs_02, file names or model ids are fine.
- Do not count sites: write "the refund planner stays on its model", not "one site stays".
- Parity is agreement with references (expected outputs built for the evaluation), never with the original model, whose outputs were not recorded: do not claim consistency or agreement with the original or prior model.
- Use only the facts given. No marketing language, no emoji.

message.content: {"summary": "This PR leaves all call sites on their current models because none of the tested alternative tiers reached the required parity with reference outputs on held-out cases, except where lint or missing edits block automation. The evidence comes from running the repository's own test suite on the proposed patches and measuring agreement with reference outputs built for evaluation.", "sites": [{"site_id": "cs_01", "note": "The triage ticket function stays on gpt-4o-mini because Lightning tier did not meet the parity threshold; the adapter changes clarified intent boundaries and added examples to improve future retraining."}, {"site_id": "cs_02", "note": "The next_action function remains on claude-sonnet-4-5 as no tier matched reference behavior closely enough; the adapter updates replaced conflicting examples with reasoning steps while preserving the function-calling directive."}, {"site_id": "cs_03", "note": "The extract_order function keeps claude-sonnet-4-5 since tested tiers fell short of parity; the adapter changes tightened field rules and prevented cross-email contamination without altering token limits."}, {"site_id": "cs_04", "note": "The answer_question function requires manual review because the automated patch produced no edit blocks, so a reviewer must assess whether any change is needed."}, {"site_id": "cs_05", "note": "The plan_refund function needs manual review due to a line-length lint failure in the patched file, which a reviewer must resolve before proceeding."}, {"site_id": "cs_06", "note": "The summarize_thread function awaits manual review as the patch contained no edit blocks, leaving the reviewer to determine if modifications are warranted."}]}
